A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L2R research. Their methods, equations, results, figures, references, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original detector evaluations across 21 domains, plus prompt-diversity and calibration-loss ablations in Figures 5–6 and Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original detector comparisons, M4 out-of-distribution evaluation, adversarial tests, and training-data, model-capacity, and generation-setting analyses, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The intended L2R procedure remains Llama-3-8B rewriting, signed cross-entropy training, threshold-based loss calibration, and classification using rewrite similarity. The added pseudocode and LoRA-capacity experiments do not establish a new core algorithm. Formal calibration-description changes are assessed under T1.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original 21 domains, adds GPT-3.5-Turbo as a fourth generator, evaluates M4 with five nonoverlapping English domains and additional generators, and uses MAGE for a training-data comparison. It also evaluates adversarially modified test texts, substantially expanding coverage beyond v1's constructed dataset.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates GPT-2 Detector, Fast-DetectGPT, and RAIDAR with Gemini or Llama rewriting. v2 removes GPT-2 Detector and adds evaluated Ghostbusters and directly fine-tuned Llama Logits baselines, while retaining Fast-DetectGPT and the rewriting comparators. Tables 3–4 also compare reduced-parameter classifier configurations.

E3.justification: v1 Table 1 describes separately trained per-domain comparisons; v2 Table 1 specifies one classifier trained across all domains. Rewriting and ablation reporting switches from accuracy/F1 to AUROC. New protocols include M4 transfer, training on clean data and testing attacked data, matched MAGE training, four LoRA configurations, and controlled length/decoding variations. The default 70/30 split remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds distribution-shift and adversarial robustness tests, a LoRA-capacity sweep, an objective-versus-direct-classification control, a MAGE training-data comparison, and text-length/decoding ablations in Appendix A.6. The existing prompt-diversity and calibration studies are retained in Appendices A.3 and A.5, with revised reporting.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.1 first explicitly states that experimental results use a single run, citing temperature-zero rewriting. v1 does not specify run counts. Both report standard deviations across domains; neither adds confidence intervals or significance tests. This is added disclosure, not evidence that the actual run count changed.

E6.justification: v1's accuracy/F1 results are replaced by AUROC reporting: its Table 1 gives L2R 0.8313 accuracy and 0.8334 F1, while v2 Table 1 reports 0.9009 AUROC. New results include M4 AUROC of 0.6561/0.7398 for full/reduced L2R and attack scores of 0.8746/0.8927. Dataset-training and generation-variation results are also added. Changed coverage, metrics, and protocols preclude treating these as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The signed-loss expression is rewritten equivalently. However, v1 Equation 3's calibration gates are replaced by Algorithm 1, whose inequalities now match the unchanged prose: human loss below the threshold and AI loss above it. This is a limited formal revision. The pseudocode still does not explicitly preserve the negative human-loss sign; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 makes adversarial robustness and better generalization than equally parameterized direct classification central abstract and contribution claims. It explicitly separates in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance claims, while dropping v1's claim to the world's most diverse dataset. The underlying learned-rewriting contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the capacity sweep as an accuracy–generalization tradeoff, attributes advantages over Llama Logits to the rewriting objective, and explains attack resistance through remaining separation between human and AI rewrite distributions. It also interprets the MAGE comparison as evidence for training-data quality. The slow-inference limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds batch size, weight decay, decoding settings, training and per-text inference times, preprocessing instructions, dataset licenses, and four LoRA configurations with parameter counts. It also specifies baseline implementations and matching procedures. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to previously unstated settings. The future release promise now includes data.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion of GLTR, PECOLA, generalization studies, and DPO, and acknowledges RAID, RuTAD, and MAGE when positioning its dataset. Dataset novelty is qualified through comparison with existing diverse datasets. The central relationship to RAIDAR and supervised versus zero-shot detection remains; publication metadata updates are not new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with an explicit contribution list. Dataset discussion becomes collection, prompt-diversity, and cleaning subsections; evaluation is reorganized around generalization and robustness. Existing ablations move into an expanded appendix, and conclusion and limitations exchange order.

P2.justification: v2 combines the earlier histograms and calibration schematic in Figure 1, adds edit counts and domain illustrations to Figure 2, and replaces the earlier comparison displays with expanded AUROC tables. It adds a capacity plot and several experimental tables. The calibration curve is redrawn, and the existing rewrite examples move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: v1's generalization claims relied mainly on testing within its constructed dataset. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through independent M4 evaluation, adversarial tests, matched direct-classification controls, and dataset/capacity ablations. It also exposes the full-model versus reduced-parameter generalization tradeoff and improves reproducibility documentation. These gains outweigh reporting problems, including the claimed 37.26% OOD advantage over Fast-DetectGPT, which conflicts with Table 3, and the unclear human-loss sign in Algorithm 1.
